title: Controls alignment and auditor Q&A runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook captures a ready-to-read control alignment (SOC2 + ISO27001) snapshot, prioritized gaps tied to RBAC v2, audit-log schema, SIEM export automation, and a practical Q&A script for auditors. Intended as a briefing doc for the audit team and as a checklist for engineers who will produce evidence during fieldwork.

High-level summary:
- Current posture: documented control mappings exist but several controls rely on manual evidence pulls (esp. RBAC change history and SIEM retention proofs).
- Risk areas: partial RBAC telemetry (missing role-change context), inconsistent audit log schema across services, ad-hoc SIEM export packaging for auditors.
- Recommended short-term fixes: standardize log enrichment (requester, change-reason, correlation_id), automate daily export snapshot to secure bucket, create canonical evidence filenames and index.

Control mapping excerpt (concise):
Format: Control ID | Control objective | Current state | Representative evidence file(s) | Gap severity | Remediation owner | ETA
- SOC2-CC6 | Access controls: restrict logical access and track changes | RBAC v2 deployed, change approvals via PR but change events not always stored in central audit-log | rbac/approvals/pr-logs-2024-*.zip; serviceX-local-audit.log | High (evidence portability) | Priya Rao | 2025-03-01
- SOC2-CC7 | System activity logging and monitoring | Services emit logs; fields vary (user_id vs email vs principal). SIEM ingests but enrichment missing correlation_id | siem/ingest-schema-v1.json; siem/export/2025-01-*.ndjson | Medium | Ethan Williams | 2025-02-15
- ISO27001-A.9.2 | User access rights review | Quarterly reviews exist but reviewer attestations are email threads, not centralized artifacts | access/review-attestations-2024-Q4.pdf | Low | Liam O'Connor | 2025-02-01

Notes on evidence packaging and naming convention (auditor-friendly):
- Canonical path: evidence/<control-id>/<artifact-type>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<service>-<artifact>.zip
- Examples: evidence/SOC2-CC6/rbac-export/2025-01-10-iam-service-export.zip ; evidence/ISO27001-A.12/siem-export/2025-01-09-siem-snapshot.ndjson
- Each archive MUST include a small text manifest (manifest.txt) listing generated_by, utc_timestamp, sha256 checksums, and a short explanation of how the artifact maps to the control.

SIEM export schema validation (practical checklist for SRE/infra):
- Required fields for exported events: utc_ts, service, env, severity, event_type, user_identity (type+id), correlation_id, request_id, request_path, outcome, actor_ip, geo (optional), raw_message
- Field harmonization: map service-specific user fields to user_identity.{type,id}. Provide a small mapping table per service.
- Retention proof: daily export snapshots for the last 90 days into secure, versioned bucket with object-level metadata: exported_by, export_range, sha256.
- Automation: cron job -> export -> validate schema (jsonschema) -> sign manifest -> copy to evidence-bucket/enforced-retention/

RBAC v2 evidence specifics (what auditors will ask & where to find it):
- Question: How are role assignments approved and recorded?
  Recommended answer: Role changes are done via the infra RBAC service; changes are made through GitOps PRs or the admin console. Approval trail: Git history + PR approvals + console-change events. Evidence files: rbac/pr-history-YYYY-MM.tar.gz, rbac/console-change-events-YYYY-MM.ndjson. If an auditor requests an example, provide 2 anonymized samples plus the corresponding PR and signed manifest.
- Question: Can you demonstrate a recent role rollback and its audit trail?
  Recommended answer: Yes — provide rollback PR, console-event, and SIEM correlation of affected sessions. Evidence files: rbac/rollback-examples/2025-01-xx-rollback.zip, siem/correlation-rollback-2025-01-xx.ndjson.

Quick-gap analysis (actionable, prioritized):
- A: Centralize RBAC event emission (high) — create event adapter in iam-service to emit canonical 'rbac_change' events with reason and actor_id. Owner: Priya. ETA: 3 weeks.
- B: Implement jsonschema validation in SIEM exporter (medium) — fail export if required fields missing and alert team. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2 weeks.
- C: Create automated evidence bundler (low-medium) — nightly job that zips required artifacts and writes manifest. Owner: SRE. ETA: 4 weeks.
- D: Standardize attestations (low) — move quarterly access reviews into a simple Confluence form that auto-generates signed PDF. Owner: Liam. ETA: 1 month.

Auditor Q&A script (verbatim-friendly, interviewer / responder format):
- Auditor: "Show me the change history for that role assignment."
  Responder: "We have a GitOps record (PR#1234) and a console event emitted at 2025-01-06T14:32:12Z. Here's a signed archive (rbac/pr-history-2025-01.tar.gz) and a manifest that ties the two. The event includes correlation_id 'c-abc123' which we can use to show related SIEM events."
- Auditor: "How do you ensure logs are complete and tamper-evident?"
  Responder: "All services push to an append-only pub/sub which the SIEM ingests. Exports are checksummed and retained in versioned object storage; manifests include sha256 checksums and exported_by. We additionally maintain a daily export log that records export success/failure; failures open an incident ticket and trigger a PagerDuty alert."
- Auditor: "Can you show that access reviews were performed?"
  Responder: "Yes — access-review-2024-Q4.pdf contains reviewer attestations. We are moving to an automated attestation workflow; current manual attestations are captured and archived with signer metadata."

Evidence collection playbook (step-by-step for engineers):
1) Identify control and required artifact list from the control matrix.
2) Run the relevant exporter (rbac/export, siem/snapshot, auditlog/collect) with the requested timeframe.
3) Validate exported files with jsonschema and checksum tools.
4) Create manifest.txt with mapping statements: which log lines map to which control test.
5) Upload to evidence-bucket/<control-id>/ and notify auditor folder (share link with expiry).
6) Add a short note in the audit tracker (JIRA-SEC-XXXX) with links to artifacts and summary.

Sample SIEM query snippets to support auditor questions (examples to run in Splunk/ELK):
- Find RBAC change events correlated to a user session:
  index=app OR index=auth event_type=rbac_change correlation_id="*" | join correlation_id [search index=app event_type=session_start] | table utc_ts, service, event_type, user_identity, correlation_id, outcome
- Show all failed login attempts prior to role change:
  index=auth event_type=failed_login user_identity.id=USERX earliest=-30d@d latest=@d | join user_identity.id [search index=app event_type=rbac_change user_identity.id=USERX earliest=-30d@d latest=@d] | stats count by event_type, user_identity.id

Appendix: artifact examples and redaction guidance:
- When sharing PRs or logs with sensitive PII: provide anonymized copies and an unredacted version in a secure view-only bucket for the auditor with an NDA/approved access list.
- Example manifest.txt content: generated_by: rbac-exporter-v2; utc_time: 2025-01-10T02:00:00Z; sha256: <hex>; maps_to: SOC2-CC6; note: includes PRs 1212,1220 and console events.

Open questions for the audit prep meeting (to resolve before fieldwork):
- Finalize canonical event field names (agree on user_identity.{type,id} and correlation_id format).
- Decide on retention proof window for SIEM (90 vs 180 days) to satisfy both legal and auditor expectations.
- Confirm whether anonymized sample artifacts suffice for initial review or if full PII-bearing artifacts will be needed on-site.

Action items (owners + near-term dates):
- Priya: RBAC event adapter spec + PR by 2025-01-22.
- Ethan: SIEM exporter jsonschema + CI validation by 2025-01-18.
- SRE (Maya): nightly evidence bundler prototype by 2025-02-01.
- Liam: migrate Q4 attestations into auto-form (Confluence) by 2025-02-20.

Contact list for fieldwork week:

- RBAC owner: Priya Rao (priya@redwood.ai)
- SIEM/observability: Ethan Williams (ethan@redwood.ai)
- SRE lead: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai)

Notes to reviewers: this is a working doc — expect iterative changes after the architecture call on 2025-01-12. Use the linked artifacts for deeper context; raise blockers in JIRA-SEC-3421.

End of runbook.
